outline.description: An overview of how modern large language models rely heavily on tokenization before feeding data into a transformer core, why this pre‑processing step introduces bias toward specific domains or modalities, and why an end‑to‑end byte‑level approach can help address these weaknesses.
subtopics: Known shortcomings—biases to language families, noise sensitivity, lack of orthographic awareness
Why scaling byte‑level models has been difficult in the past
"Dynamic compute allocation" as a central idea

outline.description: A quick refresher on sequence modeling objectives common to transformers—including causal self‑attention—and an explanation of how performance is usually measured using perplexity.
"Token” refers specifically to a byte cluster drawn from a fixed pre‑determined vocabulary whereas “patch” denotes a dynamically sized grouping created during preprocessing.
subtopics: "Differential vocabulary size" trade‑off between tokens vs patches
"Incremental” property needed when generating data token by token
